title: Cancer: current or history, and metastases
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cancer as documented at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint
Pain in lower back and hips.

HPI
Pt is an 87 y/o male with a known history of prostate carcinoma. He is currently receiving chemotherapy for management of his disease. Pt presents today c/o increased aching and stiffness in lumbar region and bilateral hips. He reports the pain is dull and constant, worsening with prolonged standing. He notes that the cancer has spread to bone, contributing to his current discomfort. Pt states he is managing symptoms but seeks better pain control.

Medication List
Lisinopril 10mg QD
Metformin 500mg BID
Acetaminophen 650mg every 6 hours PRN

Exam
General: Alert, oriented x3, in no acute distress.
Vitals: BP 132/82, HR 74, RR 16, Temp 98.6F, SpO2 97% on RA.
Musculoskeletal: Tenderness noted over lumbar spine and bilateral greater trochanters. Range of motion limited by discomfort.
Neuro: Strength 5/5 throughout. Sensation intact.

Assessment
1. Prostate cancer with bone metastases.

Plan
1. Continue current chemotherapy regimen.
2. Increase acetaminophen dose for pain management.
3. F/u in 4 weeks to monitor symptoms and side effects.

Electronically signed, R. Mensah, DO, 05/14/2026
explanations: Cancer of the prostate under current treatment is a current malignancy: C61.
Bone metastases: C79.51, secondary malignant neoplasm of bone (HCC 18, which outranks the primary-site HCC).

distractors.why: Treatment is still directed at the cancer, so it is current, not history.
Metastasis is coded as a secondary malignancy, even when the primary is history.
The metastases are in bone, not the liver.

hccs.label: Cancer Metastatic to Bone/Other and Unspecified Metastatic Cancer; Acute Leukemia Except Myeloid
